transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I don’t feel any interest in the things I used to love—my art, my garden, even time with my family just feels flat. My husband actually encouraged me to come see you because I've withdrawn so much from our daily life lately. I just don't seem to care about the things that used to define my days.
Have you felt this way consistently for at least two years, or is this a more recent change that has lasted for several weeks?

It has actually been building and sticking around for a little over two years now, rather than just being a recent change of a few weeks. It really started back when my husband began traveling frequently for work and my kids became much more independent.
During these past two years, have you experienced periods where you felt completely back to your normal self, or has this low mood and lack of interest been present most of the time?

The low, flat feelings haven't been constant and have only totaled about seven months; I actually spend much more of my time in these sped-up, high-energy phases. Even during a stretch last year when my mood felt relatively neutral, I still had the whispering and suspicious thoughts happening, so I rarely ever feel completely back to my old, normal self.
During those high-energy phases, do the whispering and suspicious thoughts persist throughout, or do they occur only during the periods when your mood is low?

Yes, they definitely happen during those high-energy phases too. In fact, some of the times when I've felt the most wired and slept the least, racing around starting projects, were also when those whispers were the loudest and I felt most convinced my family was secretly testing me.
During these high-energy phases, do you experience a significantly elevated or irritable mood, or are the psychotic symptoms and the 'wired' feeling the primary features of those periods?

It is definitely a mix of both. During those high-energy times, I feel really wired and almost giddy, but I also get incredibly irritable and snap over tiny things like how the dishwasher is loaded. Those sped-up phases are actually when the whispering and the feeling of being tested are at their absolute strongest.

During these high-energy and irritable phases, have you experienced other symptoms such as needing very little sleep, talking much faster than usual, or having racing thoughts that feel difficult to slow down?

Yes, I definitely experience all of those. During those phases, I can get by on just three or four hours of sleep and still wake up buzzing, while my mind feels like a radio stuck between stations with thoughts moving too fast to grab. I also find myself talking incredibly fast and getting easily irritated with everyone around me.
When you have those periods of low mood, do you also experience the whispering and suspicious thoughts, or do those specific symptoms only happen when you are in the high-energy, 'wired' phases?

They are actually at their loudest during those high-energy, wired phases, but I don't typically experience them when my mood is really low. There was also a stretch last year when my mood felt completely neutral, and I still heard the whispers and felt like I was being tested. So they seem to happen during the high times and the neutral times, but not the low ones.

To clarify the duration of your experiences, do you ever have these whispering or suspicious thoughts when you are not currently in a high-energy phase or a low-mood phase, and if so, for how long have they persisted in total?

Yes, I definitely experience them during neutral times; last year there was a stretch where I felt neither high nor low, but I still heard the whispers and felt like I was being tested. In total, these whispering and suspicious thoughts have been happening on and off for about a year and a half now.
During that year and a half of hearing voices and feeling suspicious, were there any periods of at least two weeks where you experienced those symptoms without any significant mood swings at all?

Yes, there was a stretch last year for a few weeks where my mood felt completely neutral—neither high nor low. Even though my mood was stable, I still heard the whispers at night and felt convinced that my husband's trips were part of a test on me.

During that period of several weeks where your mood was neutral, were the whispering and suspicious thoughts the only symptoms you experienced, or did you also have other changes in your behavior or thinking?

Yes, during those neutral weeks, the nighttime whispering and the strong feeling that my husband's trips were a test were really the main things happening. I didn't experience any of the extreme high energy, racing thoughts, or deep sadness during that time. My mood just felt mostly flat and normal, aside from those unsettling experiences.

During those weeks when your mood was neutral and you were experiencing the whispering and suspicious thoughts, did you also notice any other symptoms like social withdrawal, lack of motivation, or a decline in your ability to take care of daily tasks?

Yes, even during those neutral weeks, I still really struggled with a lack of motivation and keeping up with daily life. I continued to withdraw from my book club, let household chores slide, and missed bills and appointments. Those difficulties definitely persisted even when I wasn't experiencing the extreme emotional highs or lows.

The patient reports chronic symptoms spanning over two years, characterized by periods of high energy/decreased need for sleep (consistent with manic or hypomanic symptoms) and periods of low mood/anhedonia, both accompanied by persistent auditory hallucinations and paranoid delusions. opening_question.question: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits symptoms of both mania (elevated mood, decreased sleep, racing thoughts) and depression (anhedonia, low motivation), fulfilling criteria for schizoaffective disorder. Crucially, the presence of psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and paranoid delusions) for several weeks in the absence of mood episodes confirms the schizoaffective, mixed type diagnosis.
